candidate_windows.window_text:
The model was developed and executed on Google Colab Pro using an NVIDIA A100 GPU with driver version 533.104.05, CUDA version 12.2, system RAM of 83.5 GB, and GPU RAM of 40 GB. For efficient batch processing during the training phase, the model was trained with a batch size of 8 for 20 epochs. The implementation was carried out in the PyTorch framework, utilizing the Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2014) with an initial learning rate of $1 \times 10^{-4}$ . Performance assessment was conducted on the IEMOCAP and MERSA datasets using 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation, respectively.

We were inspired by the research of (Wang et al.,

2021) and evaluated two variants of each foundation model for feature extraction. The models we evaluated were: wav2vec 2.0-base-960 h $(\mathrm{w2v2 - b})^{1}$ , wav2vec 2.0 large $(\mathrm{w2v2 - l})^{2}$ , BERT-base $(\mathrm{BERT - b})^{3}$ , and BERT-Large $(\mathrm{BERT - l})^{4}$ , with and without the LSTM layer.
